title: `sum` of floats on the streaming engine: in turn per group, scheduling-dependent
verdict: grouped: plain left-to-right; ungrouped: pairwise per morsel, grouping varies between runs
description: On the streaming engine a grouped float `sum` adds each value in turn to its group's sum (`NumSumReducer`, `reduce_one`, `+=`), in the input's width, and adds the pipelines' partial sums on merge. With one pipeline the additions run in input order: one `Float64` group of 1e16, 1, 1, -1e16 sums to 0.0 (in memory, Kahan: 2.0), and one `Float32` group of 16777216, 1, 1 to 16777216 (in memory 16777218). A frame of 2 to 4 rows streams as one-row morsels on a 10-thread machine, so which pipelines add which rows, and in what order their partial sums merge, changes between runs. Over 200 runs on 10 threads the `Float64` group gave 2.0 92 times, 1.0 75 times and 0.0 33 times; with `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=1` or 2 it is always 0.0. The `Float32` group varies the same way (counts not recorded). The recorded results of s-group-fsum-cancel (0.0) and s-group-fsum-f32 (16777216) are one outcome among several. Each step is one IEEE addition rounded to nearest, ties to even.

Ungrouped, each morsel is summed pairwise by the in-memory kernel and added to its pipeline's running sum; which morsels a pipeline gets depends on scheduling. So the same query can give different sums from run to run: five runs of a 300 000-value sum gave 151234.90000035526 and 151234.9000003553 (in memory always the first). A grouped sum over 300 000 rows also varied between runs, on both engines (polars-exec-row-order).
The sum of no values (or only nulls) is 0. The in-memory engine's algorithms are in polars-sum-float.

Order class (streaming): (a) ungrouped, each morsel is summed by the in-memory kernel (pairwise with blocks of 128: in a block each of 16 lanes adds its 8 values in turn and the lanes reduce in a tree of depth 4, the blocks combine pairwise, and the first n mod 128 values are added in turn and then to the rest), added in turn to its pipeline's running sum, and the pipelines' sums are added in pipeline order; the morsels each pipeline gets depend on scheduling, so the tree's shape changes between runs. Grouped, each pipeline adds each row in turn to its group's sum and the pipelines' partial sums are added on merge: sequential leaves combined in an order of unknown shape. (b) Any tree: γ_h Σ|x_i| (Higham §4.2). Ungrouped, h ≤ h_morsel + M + P with h_morsel as in polars-sum-float (h ≤ max(12 + ⌈log₂ B⌉, r) for one array of n = 128B + r values (7 lane additions, 4 lane levels, ⌈log₂ B⌉ pairwise levels, the final addition; r for the leading remainder) per morsel), M the morsels of one pipeline and P the pipelines; grouped, h ≤ m − 1 + P with m the largest pipeline's row count for the group; at most n − 1 in both. u = 2⁻⁵³ for `Float64`, 2⁻²⁴ for `Float32` (summed in `f32`). (c) The source below; s-fsum-runs (two results over five runs), s-group-fsum-runs, s-group-fsum-cancel (0.0) and s-group-fsum-f32 (16777216). (d) `Float64`: ANY. Grouped with one pipeline, SEQUENTIAL in the order rows arrive; in general ANY. `Float32`: the class of ANY at u = 2⁻²⁴, which `SumOrder` (double steps) cannot express.
The docs are silent on the float summation order and its variation between runs: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins the streaming summation order; it may change between versions.
reference: `AggFn.fsum` is `floatSumCR` (D25): the exact sum of the doubles, rounded once to nearest with ties to even; a NaN, or `+∞` with `-∞`, gives NaN, and one kind of infinity gives it. NULL without values. An engine's own order of additions is within the plan's bound (`sum_order`, `StdModel.epsilon_sum_cr`).

notes: s-group-fsum-cancel: 2.0 in memory, 0.0 streaming; s-group-fsum-f32: 16777218 in memory, 16777216 streaming; s-fsum-runs: streaming gave two values over five runs, in memory one; s-group-fsum-runs varied on both engines.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: `NumSumReducer`: `reduce_one` adds a value to its group's sum; `combine` adds partial sums
ungrouped reduce: one state per pipeline, merged in turn

notes: Carried over from polars-sum-float's round-2 reading of the streaming paths, which the probes confirm.

evidence.note: horizontal sum: 16 → 8 → 4 lanes, then (v0 + v2) + (v1 + v3)
a block of 128: 16 lanes, each adding 8 values in turn
pairwise over whole blocks, split at half the blocks
the first n mod 128 values added in turn, then mainsum + restsum
ChunkAgg::sum folds the chunks' sums left; _sum_as_f64 likewise
NumSumReducer: reduce_ca adds the morsel's ChunkAgg::sum; reduce_one and combine `+=`
ungrouped: one state per pipeline, merged in pipeline order
grouped: reduce_one per row; combine_subset merges the pipelines' states
Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms (2nd ed., SIAM 2002), ch. 4 Summation: §4.2 recursive, pairwise and any-order bounds; §4.3 compensated summation

provenance.notes: Rerun on small inputs (3,000 or 5,000 rows) in a subprocess with POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=64 and POLARS_SORT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES=1024, which Polars reads at start-up: the same behaviour as the large inputs at the defaults (the unstable streaming sort, sums and var varying by run), so the probes stay cheap. The variables only move the thresholds; the large-input results at the defaults stand.
